method: Payload hash for sig_version 1 is SHA-256 of payload_json.
Each link prev equals the previous payload_hash. Link 1 has no prev.
OpenPGP statements are ASCII-armored signed messages. GnuPG decrypts them and the plaintext must equal payload_json.
NaCl sig_version 1 signs payload_json with Ed25519. The public key is the 32 bytes inside the KID.
NaCl sig_version 2 signs a msgpack array that contains the seqno, the previous payload hash, and SHA-256 of payload_json. payload_hash is SHA-256 of that array.
A NaCl sig_id is SHA-256 of the decoded signature blob plus one suffix byte. 0x0f is the user-signature suffix. 0x22 is the suffix Keybase uses for a sig_version 2 wallet.stellar link.
A signing subkey that has since expired still counts as a good historical signature when GnuPG reports GOODSIG.
The Keybase daemon was not started. This check does not ask keybase.io to re-validate remote proofs.
A Keybase cryptocurrency statement does not prove spend control of that address.
